function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle Corporation). It was designed to have the following key characteristics:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java programs are compiled into bytecode, which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The same bytecode can run on any device that has a JVM implementation, making Java “write once, run anywhere.” |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything in Java is an object (except primitive types). This encourages modular, reusable code. |
| **Strongly typed** | Variables must be declared with a type, and type checking occurs at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Java uses garbage collection to automatically reclaim memory that is no longer referenced, relieving developers from manual memory deallocation. |
| **Rich standard library** | The Java Standard Edition (SE) includes libraries for collections, networking, I/O, concurrency, GUI (Swing, AWT), and more. |
| **Multithreading support** | Java has built‑in support for concurrent programming, making it suitable for high‑performance applications. |
| **Security** | The JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and security manager help protect against malicious code. |

### Typical Use Cases

| Domain | Typical Java Applications |
|--------|---------------------------|
| **Enterprise software** | Web services, microservices, batch processing, ERP systems |
| **Mobile** | Android apps (Android SDK uses Java or Kotlin) |
| **Web** | Servlets, JSP, Spring MVC, JavaServer Faces (JSF) |
| **Desktop** | Swing, JavaFX, IDEs (Eclipse, IntelliJ IDEA) |
| **Embedded systems** | IoT devices, automotive software |
| **Scientific computing** | Numerical libraries, data analysis tools |
| **Cloud & Big Data** | Hadoop, Spark (Java APIs), distributed systems |

### Core Components

1. **JDK (Java Development Kit)** – Includes the compiler (`javac`), JVM, and core libraries.
2. **JRE (Java Runtime Environment)** – Contains the JVM and core libraries needed to run Java applications.
3. **JVM (Java Virtual Machine)** – Executes bytecode and manages memory, threads, and native calls.

### Example

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, world!");
    }
}
```

Compile with `javac HelloWorld.java`, then run with `java HelloWorld`. The same bytecode will run on any platform with a compatible JVM.

---

**Bottom line:** Java is a versatile, widely‑used programming language that emphasizes portability, robustness, and a rich ecosystem of libraries and frameworks. It powers everything from enterprise back‑ends to Android mobile apps and is a staple in many software development environments.
